rows.name: OAI.SKValue.spin
rows.annotation: The two cases of `spin` send `true` to $1$ and `false` to $-1$, so a Boolean configuration represents exactly the allowed signs.

rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.spinDisorder
rows.annotation: The product measure gives independent $\mathcal N(0,1)$ coordinates to all ordered pairs in `Fin n × Fin n`, including diagonal pairs. Only coordinates with $i<j$ enter `spinHamiltonian`, yielding one coupling per unordered pair.

rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.spinHamiltonian
rows.annotation: The guard `if i < j` keeps exactly one term per unordered pair in the double sum, with Boolean spins converted to $\pm1$. Division by `Real.sqrt n` supplies the displayed normalisation.

rows.fidelity_note: The Lean formula allows every nonnegative variance t; the paper uses its variance-one specialization.
rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.Heat.heatKernel_formula
rows.annotation: Setting $t=1$ in `heatKernel_formula` gives the paper’s standard normal density. At $t=0$ Lean’s division convention makes the formula zero, so the density interpretation here is for $t>0$.

rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.Gaussian.gaussian_abs_moment
rows.annotation: The case $v=1$ gives $\mathbb E|Z|=\sqrt{2/\pi}$, while the statement covers every variance $v\ge0$. The intermediate equality with twice the integral over the positive half-line is not stated here.

rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.expectedSKMaximum
rows.annotation: For each fixed `J`, `Set.range (spinHamiltonian n J)` ranges over configurations before `sSup` is taken. The integral then averages that optimum under `spinDisorder n`, and division by $n$ gives energy per spin.

rows.fidelity_note: This defines the finite expected optimum per spin; it does not state the n-to-infinity limit.
rows.name: OAI.SKValue.groundStateSequence
rows.annotation: The factor $(n:\mathbb R)^{-1}$ normalises the expected maximum at each finite $n$, with maximisation inside the disorder integral. This defines the sequence whose limit appears in the passage, without asserting convergence.

rows.name: OAI.SKValue.groundStateValue
rows.annotation: The filter `atTop` sends the natural system size $n$ to infinity. `limUnder` defines `groundStateValue`, while convergence to that value is a separate assertion.

rows.name: OAI.SKValueG.groundStateSequence_tendsto
rows.annotation: The `Tendsto` conclusion asserts actual convergence of the finite expected energies per spin to `groundStateValue` as $n\to\infty$. The proof applies the subadditive limit theorem to the negative expected maxima.

rows.annotation: For every $t\in[0,1)$, the constructed `parameterMeasure γ` has mass $\gamma(t)$ on $[0,t]$. The proof adds its Stieltjes part's mass $\gamma(t)-\gamma(0)$ to the atom at zero.

rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.IsStieltjesMeasure
rows.annotation: Since `Time` starts at zero, `Iic t` is $[0,t]$, and `ENNReal.ofReal` converts the nonnegative value $\gamma(t)$ to a measure value. This predicate imposes the first displayed equality on a supplied measure, with the increment formula a separate consequence.

rows.fidelity_note: This theorem gives the increment identity, assuming `hμ` already supplies the cumulative relation; it does not assert existence of the measure.
rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.SupportDeterministic.IsStieltjesMeasure.cdf_add_Ioc
rows.annotation: The decomposition $[0,b]=[0,a]\cup(a,b]$ gives the additive identity in `ENNReal` for $a\le b$. The measure is supplied through `hμ`, and for admissible $\gamma$ this rearranges to $\mu((a,b])=\gamma(b)-\gamma(a)$.

rows.fidelity_note: Lean proves finite mass on every compact subset of $[0,1)$, including each $[0,T]$ with $T<1$.
rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.SupportDeterministic.IsStieltjesMeasure.finiteOnCompacts
rows.annotation: The proof bounds a nonempty compact set by $[0,b]$ at its maximum $b<1$. The cumulative identity `hμ b` makes that interval's mass finite, without any assumption of finite total mass.

rows.fidelity_note: The integrable field supplies finite area of $\gamma$, but not the equality to the weighted Stieltjes integral.
rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.OrderParameter
rows.annotation: The field `integrable` requires integrability of `extend val` on $\mathbb R$. Since this extension is nonnegative and zero outside $[0,1)$, it ensures finite area under $\gamma$, without stating the weighted Stieltjes identity.

rows.fidelity_note: Lean assumes `[IsFiniteMeasure ν]`; the paper allows $\mu_\gamma([0,1))$ to be infinite. A limiting or nonnegative-integral argument is needed for the full weighted identity.

rows.annotation: Taking $H=1$ makes the inner integral $1-r$ and gives the weighted identity for `finiteCDF ν`. The hypothesis `[IsFiniteMeasure ν]` restricts this row to finite total mass, whereas the paper allows infinite total mass.

rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.finiteCDF_fubini
rows.plain: Changing integration order for finite mass
rows.annotation: The proof expands the cumulative mass using the indicator of $r\leq t$, then interchanges the integrals. The signature makes finiteness of $\nu$ and integrability of $H$ available for that signed interchange.

rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.Time
rows.annotation: `Time` is the subtype `Ico (0 : ℝ) 1`, so it contains zero and only times strictly below one. A measure on that type can have an initial atom at zero.

rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.SupportDeterministic.InSupport
rows.annotation: The existential condition first requires $t\in[0,1)$, then tests the corresponding point in the support of a measure on `Time`. This support uses relative neighbourhoods, including one-sided neighbourhoods at zero.

rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.SupportDeterministic.IsStieltjesMeasure.lt_cdf_of_full_support
rows.annotation: The proof puts the midpoint of $a<b$ in `μ.support`, giving positive mass to $(a,b)$ and hence to $(a,b]$. Combining this with the cumulative identity `hμ` yields $\gamma(a)<\gamma(b)$.

ties.plain: Zero interval mass gives equal values

rows.fidelity_note: The lemma gives zero mass on (a,b] implies equal cumulative values. The paper also takes the contrapositive and chooses a smaller interval inside each neighbourhood to conclude support membership.
rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.SupportDeterministic.IsStieltjesMeasure.eq_cdf_of_measure_Ioc_zero
rows.plain: Zero interval mass gives equal values
rows.annotation: Under `hγ` and $a\le b$, zero mass on $(a,b]$ forces $\gamma(a)=\gamma(b)$, so a strict increment implies positive interval mass by contraposition. Locating such an interval inside each neighbourhood is an additional step beyond this lemma.

rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.controlPayoff
rows.annotation: The outer absolute value applies to the terminal state obtained from $x$ after Brownian noise and control drift. It implements the terminal reward, while the quadratic integral subtracts the running cost and the one-spin maximisation identity is not stated here.

rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.BrownianSystem
rows.annotation: The field `brownian` imposes `IsBrownianReal B law`, including continuous paths starting at zero almost surely and independent Gaussian increments. The separate fields `isProbability` and `measurable` require a probability law and measurable evaluations at each nonnegative time.

rows.fidelity_note: The theorem handles every constant terminal coefficient $c\ge0$. With $\gamma=0$ and $c=0$ its `varianceLogHeat` expression reduces to the stated Gaussian average for $0\le t<1$.
rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.value_on_terminal_plateau
rows.plain: Value on a constant terminal interval
rows.annotation: For the zero candidate, take $c=0$, so `varianceLogHeat` reduces to the Gaussian average of `abs` with variance $1-t$. The theorem assumes $0\le t<1$ and a constant coefficient on $(a,1)$ with $a<t$, and also covers positive $c$.

rows.fidelity_note: The uniform two-sided bound holds for every $0\le t\le1$; at $t=1$ both error terms vanish, giving the paper’s terminal equality.
rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.value_terminal_uniform
rows.annotation: At $t=1$, both the square-root term and the integral from $t$ to one vanish. The two inequalities then force `value W γ 1 x` to equal $|x|$ for every admissible $\gamma$.

rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.Control
rows.annotation: The argument of `val` is elapsed time since the starting time `t`. Its `progressive` field restricts responses to the filtration of increments $B_{t+s}-B_t$, and `bound` enforces $|\alpha_s|\le1$ for every time and path.

rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.value
rows.annotation: The range inside `sSup` consists of expected `controlPayoff` values, one for each `Control W (Real.toNNReal t)`. Thus expectation is taken for a fixed permitted rule before maximising over rules.

rows.fidelity_note: This declaration gives the pathwise score inside the expectation; the separate value definition takes expectation and the supremum over permitted controls.
rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.controlPayoff
rows.annotation: This is the pathwise reward minus cost, before `value` takes expectation and a supremum. The expression `α.val (Real.toNNReal (s - t)) ω` converts the paper's response at absolute time $s$ into the control's indexing by elapsed time.

rows.fidelity_note: The declaration constructs the information filtration; the progressive requirement itself is the progressive field of Control.
rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.incrementFiltration
rows.annotation: At elapsed time $s$, this is the natural filtration generated by the increment process $r\mapsto B_{t+r}-B_t$ up to $r=s$. The requirement that a control be progressive with respect to it is imposed in `Control`.

rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.Control
rows.annotation: The `progressive` field requires joint measurability in elapsed time and path on each interval $[0,s]$, using the increment information available at $s$. The additional `bound` field restricts responses to $[-1,1]$.

rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.parisi
rows.annotation: The term `value W γ 0 0` fixes the initial time and state, and the subtraction is half the time-weighted area under $\gamma$.

rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.parisi
rows.annotation: The factor `t * extend γ.val t` is the integrand $t\gamma(t)$. Setting the extension to zero at the excluded endpoint one leaves the displayed Lebesgue integral unchanged.

rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.IsMinimizer
rows.annotation: In `IsMinimizer` the variable `η` ranges over all `OrderParameter` values. The inequality compares the Parisi value at the supplied `γ` with every admissible competitor.

rows.fidelity_note: Lean assumes `hmin : IsMinimizer W γ` and proves equality for that supplied $\gamma$. The displayed minimum also asserts attainment, which this theorem does not establish.
rows.name: OAI.SKValue.ground_state_parisi_target
rows.plain: The Parisi functional at a minimiser equals the ground-state value
rows.annotation: `ground_state_parisi_target` takes a minimiser as data through `hmin` and identifies its scalar Parisi value with $P_*$. The paper cites the Parisi theorem for the minimum formula and attainment.

rows.fidelity_note: This theorem proves only $P_*\le\mathcal P(\gamma)$ for every candidate; it neither supplies a minimiser nor proves the reverse inequality by itself.
rows.name: OAI.SKValue.groundStateValue_le_parisi
rows.plain: Each admissible Parisi value bounds the ground-state value above
rows.annotation: The proof passes an upper bound for the finite systems to their limit. For every supplied scalar-model coefficient it obtains the direction $P_*\leq\mathcal P(\gamma)$ of the displayed minimum formula.

ties.plain: Each admissible Parisi value bounds the ground-state value above

rows.name: OAI.SKValue.groundStateValue_le_parisi
rows.plain: Each admissible Parisi value bounds the ground-state value above
rows.annotation: No minimality hypothesis appears, so the bound applies to every admissible $\gamma$. The inequality runs from `groundStateValue` to `parisi W γ`, making the latter an upper bound on the limiting optimum.

rows.annotation: `hmin : IsMinimizer W γ` is a premise. The measure and process constructed in `FullSupportConclusion` are associated to that chosen order parameter.

ties.plain: Value changes no faster than distance

rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.value_lipschitz
rows.plain: Value changes no faster than distance
rows.annotation: For fixed $t\le1$, `LipschitzWith 1` is exactly $|\Phi_\gamma(t,x)-\Phi_\gamma(t,y)|\le|x-y|$ for all real $x,y$. The statement includes $t=1$ and has no hypothesis bounding $t$ below.

rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.value_convex
rows.annotation: The domain `Set.univ` makes this convexity in the spatial variable over all $\mathbb R$, for fixed $t\le1$. The proof bounds each control's payoff at a convex combination by its endpoint payoffs, then bounds those by the endpoint values of `value`.

ties.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.expected_controlPayoff_convex
ties.plain: Fixed control gives convex expected payoff

rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.expected_controlPayoff_convex
rows.plain: Fixed control gives convex expected payoff
rows.annotation: With `α` fixed, the Brownian increment and control drift translate the absolute-value function of $x$, while the cost is constant in $x$. The proof integrates this convex function, using $t\le1$ to obtain integrability.

rows.fidelity_note: Lean proves infinite spatial differentiability for $0\le t<1$; the phrase asks only for spatial differentiability.
rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.value_contDiff
rows.annotation: The expression `value W γ t` fixes time and leaves $x$ as its argument, so `ContDiff ℝ ∞` gives all spatial derivatives for $0\le t<1$. It asserts neither time differentiability nor smoothness at $t=1$.

rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.gradient
rows.annotation: Applying `deriv` to `value W γ t` differentiates its remaining argument `x`. The other arguments `W`, `γ` and `t` stay fixed, giving the spatial slope $u(t,x)$.

rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.curvature
rows.annotation: This differentiates `gradient W γ t` in its remaining spatial argument, giving `deriv (deriv (value W γ t)) x` after unfolding `gradient`. Time and the order parameter stay fixed in both derivatives.

rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.gradient_abs_le_one
rows.annotation: `value_lipschitz` supplies the bound on Lean’s total derivative `gradient` for all $t\leq1$. The inclusion of terminal time is a bound on `deriv` under Lean’s convention at a nondifferentiable point.

rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.curvature_nonneg
rows.annotation: For $0\le t<1$, convexity and spatial differentiability make `gradient W γ t` monotone. The proof takes its nonnegative derivative, which is `curvature W γ t x`.

ties.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.WeakIto.exists_feedback_verification
ties.plain: Approximate feedback on a smooth strip

rows.fidelity_note: The Lean lemma assumes a smooth constant-coefficient finite-horizon PDE and returns an $\varepsilon$-optimal bounded progressive control. It does not state exact attainment by the slope feedback for every integrable order parameter.
rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.WeakIto.exists_feedback_verification
rows.plain: Approximate feedback on a smooth strip
rows.annotation: With constant $c\geq0$ and the PDE and regularity hypotheses, each $\varepsilon>0$ gives a bounded progressive control attaining at least $F(0,x)-\varepsilon$ in expected terminal reward minus cost. The conclusion is approximate optimality for this constant-coefficient problem.

rows.fidelity_note: The lemma states an integrated upper bound under $a\le b$, $c\ge0$ and integrability assumptions; it does not state the displayed pointwise algebraic identity.
rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.WeakIto.integrated_completion_square
rows.annotation: For constants $c\ge0$ and $u$, the lemma integrates the inequality obtained by completing the square over $[a,b]$ with $a\le b$, assuming both `α` and its square are integrable. It gives the upper bound $(b-a)cu^2/2$, without retaining the square remainder in the displayed identity.

rows.fidelity_note: The identity gives equality after substituting $v=u$ (with a step factor $h$), not the full square-completion identity for arbitrary $v$.
rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.WeakIto.completion_square_feedback
rows.plain: The slope response attains quadratic equality
rows.annotation: Lean takes the special choice $v=u$ and includes a factor $h$ for the time step. With that choice the square in the paper vanishes and the drift term minus cost is $chu^2/2$.

rows.fidelity_note: The lemma gives the integrated upper bound for a fixed u; it does not itself assert attainment by a permitted stochastic control.
rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.WeakIto.integrated_completion_square
rows.annotation: For constant $u$, nonnegative $c$ and $a\leq b$, Lean integrates the upper bound with `α` and its square assumed integrable. The estimate is the payoff comparison, before choosing a progressive control.

rows.fidelity_note: The lemma gives the equality after choosing the response $u$. Feasibility $|u|\le1$ and maximality under $\gamma\ge0$ use the surrounding argument.
rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.WeakIto.completion_square_feedback
rows.plain: The slope response attains quadratic equality
rows.annotation: The response has already been set equal to $u$ on the left, and the identity computes its gain as $hcu^2/2$. The identity assumes neither $|u|\le1$ nor $c\ge0$, so feasibility and the upper bound require the surrounding argument.

rows.fidelity_note: The definition includes the $\gamma u^2/2$ term in the time equation. It does not state sensitivity to $\gamma$ or the first-variation formula.
rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.valueRate
rows.annotation: `valueRate` is a rate in time, defined as $-a(t,x)/2-\gamma(t)u(t,x)^2/2$. The squared slope is the term multiplied by the order parameter in the PDE.

rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.IsDiffusion
rows.annotation: The quantifier `∀ᵐ ω` precedes the time quantifier, so the equation holds simultaneously at every time in $[0,1]$ outside one null set, together with continuity and $X_0=0$. Progressive measurability is a separate conjunct.

rows.fidelity_note: This theorem constructs a process satisfying IsDiffusion; it does not assert uniqueness.
rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.diffusion_isDiffusion
rows.annotation: The constructed `diffusion W γ` satisfies `IsDiffusion`, giving a solution for each $W,\gamma$, including the equation through $t=1$. Comparison with another solution is a separate uniqueness statement.

rows.fidelity_note: This theorem proves almost-sure uniqueness for a supplied process hX using the same W; it does not construct the process.
rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.diffusion_uniqueness
rows.plain: Uniqueness for the same Brownian noise
rows.annotation: `hX` is a diffusion hypothesis for the same `W` and `γ` used by `diffusion W γ`. The two processes agree outside one null set simultaneously for all $0\leq t\leq1$.

rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.eulerState
rows.annotation: With $h=T/N$, `meshTime T N j` is $jh$. The successor clause adds $h\gamma(jh)u(jh,X_j)$ and $\sqrt h Z_j$ to the previous `eulerState`, with $Z_j$ given by `gaussianCoordinate N j z`.

rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.eulerState
rows.annotation: The response is computed from the state at index $j$, which uses only earlier Gaussian coordinates. The new `gaussianCoordinate N j z` is added separately and never enters the `gradient` argument.

rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.squareMoment
rows.annotation: The integrand is the square of `gradient` evaluated at `X (Real.toNNReal t) ω`, and `W.law` supplies the expectation. The definition accepts any process `X`, with no diffusion hypothesis.

ties.plain: Derivative of the mean squared response

rows.fidelity_note: This theorem states $q'=\mathbb E[a^2]$ for $0\le t<1$, including the right derivative at zero; it does not separately assert $q(0)=0$, the bounds or derivative continuity.
rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.squareMoment_hasDerivWithinAt
rows.plain: Derivative of the mean squared response
rows.annotation: The derivative value is `curvatureMoment W γ t`, namely $\mathbb E[a(t,X_t)^2]$, for $0\le t<1$. For the derivation of the moment identity by Itô’s rule, see Section 7.2.

rows.fidelity_note: This theorem supplies only $q(0)=0$ for the associated diffusion.
rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.squareMoment_zero
rows.annotation: Rewriting with `squareMoment_eq_integral_curvatureMoment` reduces $q(0)$ to an integral from zero to zero. This establishes the initial-value clause for `diffusion W γ`.

rows.fidelity_note: This theorem supplies only $0\le q(t)\le1$ (in fact for $t\le1$), not differentiability or the derivative formula.
rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.squareMoment_bounds
rows.annotation: The first conjunct makes the absolute-value bound in the second equivalent to $q(t)\le1$. The only time hypothesis is $t\le1$, so the estimate also includes $t=1$.

rows.fidelity_note: This theorem supplies continuity of $\mathbb E[a^2]$ on $[0,1)$; the derivative theorem is additionally needed to conclude $q$ is $C^{1}$.
rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.curvatureMoment_continuousOn_unit
rows.annotation: The function in `ContinuousOn` is the mean squared curvature, on $[0,1)$. Together with its identification as the derivative of `squareMoment`, this gives the derivative continuity required for $q\in C^1$.

ties.plain: Derivative of the mean squared response

rows.fidelity_note: `HasDerivWithinAt` gives a derivative within $[0,\infty)$, hence the right derivative at zero; continuity of that derivative is supplied by a separate theorem.
rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.squareMoment_hasDerivWithinAt
rows.plain: Derivative of the mean squared response
rows.annotation: The set `Ici (0:ℝ)` restricts difference quotients to nonnegative times, giving the right derivative at zero and the ordinary derivative for $0<t<1$. Continuity of the derivative requires the separate continuity result for `curvatureMoment`.

rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.curvatureMoment_continuousOn_unit
rows.annotation: No continuity hypothesis on $\gamma$ is added to its admissibility conditions. The conclusion makes `curvatureMoment`, identified with $q'$ by the moment derivative theorem, continuous on $[0,1)$ even across interior jumps of $\gamma$.

rows.annotation: The conclusion `Function.Even (value W γ t)` means $\Phi_\gamma(t,-x)=\Phi_\gamma(t,x)$ for every $x$. The time hypotheses include both endpoints $t=0$ and $t=1$.

rows.annotation: The proof specialises `gradient_odd` at $x=0$, forcing $u(t,0)=-u(t,0)$ for $0\le t<1$. The diffusion's initial state and the resulting $q(0)=0$ are additional steps.

rows.annotation: The zero condition concerns `squareMoment` along the constructed diffusion at time zero. The state is then zero and the slope at that state is zero by symmetry.

rows.fidelity_note: The definition is the tail integral of $q(t)-t$. It does not establish its first-variation interpretation, including the factor $1/2$ appearing in that derivative.

rows.annotation: The lower integration limit `s` expresses the tail over which added mass changes the coefficient, and the integrand is $q(t)-t$ for `diffusion W γ`. This defines $G(s)$ without the factor $1/2$ or a first-variation identity.

rows.annotation: `∀ η : OrderParameter` ranges over every admissible competitor. Global minimality then lets the variation proof take a chord toward any one such competitor.

rows.note: Full support is a conclusion under `hmin`, with `Time` equal to $[0,1)$.
rows.annotation: `FullSupportConclusion` says every measure satisfying `IsStieltjesMeasure γ μ` has `μ.support = Set.univ`. The type `Time` already restricts the statement to the relative topology of $[0,1)$.

rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.stripThird_eq_actual
rows.note: The integrand is $R_c$; `actualJet` orders 2, 3, 4 are $a, b, d$.
rows.annotation: The `actualJet` arguments of orders $2,3,4$ evaluate $a,b,d$ along the diffusion, making the integrand exactly $R_c(t,X_t)$. This identifies `stripThird` with its expectation for $0\le t\le T<1$ and arbitrary real $c$, without identifying it with $q'''$.

ties.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.Certificate.pointwise_coercivity
ties.plain: The flux-corrected expression is bounded below by κv⁴ under the sign conditions

rows.fidelity_note: The algebraic declaration assumes seven sign inequalities and proves a corrected inequality in rescaled jet variables. It does not construct the SK correction C or prove its expectation is zero.
rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.Certificate.pointwise_coercivity
rows.plain: The flux-corrected expression is bounded below by κv⁴ under the sign conditions
rows.annotation: Under the seven displayed nonnegativity hypotheses, the conclusion bounds $z^2-12Rvb^2+6v^4$ minus `WF₂` below by $\frac{1661507}{1521000000}v^4$. The connection to $C$ and its zero expectation must be established separately.

rows.fidelity_note: The polynomial identity holds for arbitrary real variables and does not supply the sign conditions making the weighted terms nonnegative.
rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.Certificate.rational_identity
rows.annotation: The right-hand side retains `WF₂` alongside a square, `weightedSquares`, `remainder` and two products whose signs depend on the variables. The identity holds for arbitrary real arguments, so using these terms for a lower bound requires separate sign hypotheses. The full polynomial identity is Equation (5) of the short paper.

rows.fidelity_note: The remainder bound assumes R,K,v,B,j are nonnegative and controls only the remainder, not every term of the corrected expression.
rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.Certificate.remainder_lower_bound
rows.plain: The remainder contains at least (1661507/1521000000)v⁴ under the sign conditions
rows.annotation: In `remainder`, $\frac{1661507}{1521000000}v^4$ is an explicit summand and every other monomial has a positive rational coefficient. Nonnegativity of $R,K,v,B,j$ allows those other summands to be discarded, with $B=b-2v$ in the certificate identity.

rows.fidelity_note: This declaration only compares the exact rational coefficient with $1/1000$; the algebraic decomposition and analytic hypotheses are separate.
rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.Certificate.coercivity_constant
rows.annotation: The strict comparison of rational numbers permits replacing $\frac{1661507}{1521000000}v^4$ by the weaker lower bound $v^4/1000$, since $v^4\ge0$.

ties.name: OAI.SKValue.integral_flux_zero
ties.plain: Zero integral of the derivative of an integrable primitive continuous at zero

rows.fidelity_note: The flux lemma assumes that both flux and derivative are integrable. It does not construct the density bounds or prove the zero-mean correction for this SK density.
rows.name: OAI.SKValue.integral_flux_zero
rows.plain: Zero integral of the derivative of an integrable primitive continuous at zero
rows.annotation: With $f$ as the flux and $g$ its derivative away from $0$, continuity of $f$ at $0$ and integrability of both functions give $\int_{\mathbb R}g=0$. Vanishing flux limits at both infinities are derived within the proof, so an SK application must supply the stated continuity, derivative and integrability conditions.

ties.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.stripThird_coercive
ties.plain: Third-order lower bound c² E[a⁴]/1000 at continuity points with c > 0

rows.fidelity_note: Lean proves the scaled inequality $\frac{\gamma(t)^4\mathbb E[a^4]}{1000}\le\gamma(t)^2\,\mathrm{stripThird}$ at a positive continuity point $t\le T<1$. The displayed $q'''$ identity and zero-mean correction are separate steps; division uses $c>0$.
rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.stripThird_coercive
rows.plain: Third-order lower bound c² E[a⁴]/1000 at continuity points with c > 0
rows.annotation: Using `stripThird_eq_actual`, the scaled bound becomes $c^4\mathbb E[a^4]/1000\le c^2\mathbb E[R_c]$ for $0<t\le T<1$ with $c=\gamma(t)$ and $\gamma$ continuous at $t$. Division by $c^2$ requires $c>0$, and the $q'''$ identity and zero-mean correction require separate results.

ties.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.positiveGamma_L1

rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.positiveGamma_L1
rows.plain: Positive step coefficients converge to the order parameter in L¹
rows.annotation: The integral compares `positiveGamma γ n` to `extend γ.val`. The latter is $\gamma$ on $[0,1)$ and its zero extension is harmless for the $L^1$ error over the time interval.

rows.fidelity_note: The Lean approximants are `approxCoeff γ n (min j n) + approxMesh n`. Their positive mesh offset changes a sampled plateau height $c$; they are not the plateau-preserving approximants described here.
rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.positiveCoeff
rows.annotation: Even if the sampled value is $c$, `positiveCoeff` adds `approxMesh n`. The paper’s local construction instead fixes the approximating coefficient at $c$ near the evaluation time.

rows.fidelity_note: Lean proves only that the sampled heights tend to $\gamma(t)$ at a continuity point. It does not assert equality to $c$ on any neighbourhood at any finite approximation index.
rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.positiveCoeff_sample_limit
rows.plain: Sampled heights converge to the coefficient
rows.annotation: By `positiveCoeff_sample_eq`, the sampled coefficient is $\gamma$ at `sampleTime n t` plus `approxMesh n`. Continuity at $t$ and the mesh tending to zero give the stated limit, without asserting that a neighbourhood has height $c$ at any finite stage.

ties.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.positiveValue_derivative_uniform
ties.plain: Uniform convergence of positive-step spatial derivatives below time one

rows.fidelity_note: Lean proves uniform convergence for every fixed natural-number derivative order $m$ on $0\le t\le T<1$, beyond the four orders required here.
rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.positiveValue_derivative_uniform
rows.plain: Uniform convergence of positive-step spatial derivatives below time one
rows.annotation: For each fixed derivative order $m$, the convergence is uniform simultaneously over $t\in[0,T]$ and all $x\in\mathbb R$, with $0\le T<1$. Orders through four are included, but uniformity over all orders or up to terminal time $1$ is not asserted.

ties.plain: Coupled states converge at sampled times

rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.positivePath_sample_limit
rows.note: At the fixed time chosen above, sampled states converge almost surely.
rows.plain: Coupled states converge at sampled times
rows.annotation: At each fixed $t\in[0,1)$, `positivePath` evaluated at `sampleNNTime n t` converges almost surely to `diffusion` at $t$. These mesh times approach $t$ from below or equal it, and the exceptional null set may depend on the fixed time.

ties.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.actual_coercivity
ties.plain: Quartic bound c² E[a⁴]/1000 at a positive continuity time

rows.fidelity_note: Lean proves the limiting inequality at every positive continuity point of an admissible coefficient, not only at points in a constant interval.
rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.actual_coercivity
rows.plain: Quartic bound c² E[a⁴]/1000 at a positive continuity time
rows.annotation: In `actual_coercivity` the two integrals converge separately by `sampleQuartic_integral_limit` and `sampleCoercive_integral_limit`. Passing the inequality to the limit requires positive time and continuity of $\gamma$ there. For the use of this inequality at a smooth minimiser to prove strictly positive density away from zero, see Section 9.2 of the long record.

rows.fidelity_note: The declaration proves $\mathbb E[a^4]>0$ for every admissible coefficient and every positive time below one, without a positive-plateau or minimiser assumption.
rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.actualQuartic_pos
rows.annotation: The fourth moment is positive because the curvature is nonzero somewhere and the diffusion law gives positive mass to every open interval. The proof applies to any admissible $\gamma$ at $0<t<1$.

rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.OrderParameter.addCDF
rows.note: Add the finite measure $\varepsilon\delta_{1/2}$; the exercise evaluates its cumulative function.
rows.annotation: Taking $\nu=\varepsilon\delta_{1/2}$ with $\varepsilon\ge0$ makes `finiteCDF ν t` equal to $\varepsilon$ for $1/2\le t<1$ and zero for $0\le t<1/2$, since `Iic t` includes the atom at the jump. The returned `OrderParameter` includes proofs of nonnegativity, monotonicity, right continuity and integrability.

rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.OrderParameter.removeCDF
rows.note: For $0<\varepsilon<1$, $\varepsilon\delta_{1/4}$ is dominated by the exercise’s original Stieltjes measure.
rows.annotation: To remove $\varepsilon\delta_{1/4}$, `hμ` must identify $\mu$ as a Stieltjes measure of $\gamma$ and `hν` must establish $\varepsilon\delta_{1/4}\le\mu$. Subtracting `finiteCDF` lowers the height by $\varepsilon$ for $1/4\le t<1$, including the jump itself, while measure domination ensures that the result remains nondecreasing.

rows.fidelity_note: The exercise scales by $1-\varepsilon$ with $0<\varepsilon<1$. The declaration permits the whole closed interval $0\le\varepsilon\le1$ and a chord toward any admissible $\beta$; choose $\beta=0$ here.
rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.OrderParameter.chord
rows.annotation: Choosing $\beta$ to be the zero order parameter makes `val` equal to $(1-\varepsilon)\gamma(t)$, scaling both atom weights by the same factor. The hypothesis `hε` permits the closed range $0\le\varepsilon\le1$, including the original coefficient and complete removal of its weights.

rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.gradient_abs_le_one
rows.annotation: The proof bounds `gradient` using the spatial Lipschitz constant $1$ of `value`, for every $x$ and $t\le1$. Squaring and averaging along $X_t$ gives $q(t)\le1$, the exact cap violated by the proposed polynomial.

rows.name: OAI.SKValue.scalar_value_target
rows.note: For a minimiser and associated diffusion, the terminal covariance is a ground-state value formula.
rows.annotation: `ScalarValueConclusion` gives a terminal witness `U` for the scalar-model slope and equates $P_*$ to its expectation paired with $B_1$. The almost-sure and mean-square limits identify the same witness.

ties.name: OAI.SKValue.ScalarValueConclusion
ties.plain: The terminal spin has Brownian correlation equal to the scalar ground-state value

rows.name: OAI.SKValue.ScalarValueConclusion
rows.note: The scalar value integrates E[a], with no square on a.
rows.plain: The terminal spin has Brownian correlation equal to the scalar ground-state value
rows.annotation: The equality containing `curvature` expresses `groundStateValue` as $\int_0^1\mathbb E[a(t,X_t)]\,dt$, with no square on $a$. The final clause requires interval integrability of this first-moment function. For the distinction between the slope martingale’s quadratic variation and its covariation with Brownian motion, see Section 5.1 of the short paper.

ties.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.FullSupportConclusion
ties.plain: Full Stieltjes support, strict increase and moment identities on [0,1)

rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.FullSupportConclusion
rows.note: The full-support conclusion uses the squared curvature moment for $0\le t<1$.
rows.plain: Full Stieltjes support, strict increase and moment identities on [0,1)
rows.annotation: For every `X` satisfying `IsDiffusion` and every `t : Time`, the last equality squares `curvature` inside the integral to give $\mathbb E[a(t,X_t)^2]=1$. The preceding `squareMoment` equality squares the slope and gives $\mathbb E[u(t,X_t)^2]=t$.

rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.full_support
rows.annotation: The last three parts of `FullSupportConclusion` give support, strict increase and the moment equalities. The moment equalities are stated for any associated diffusion, and the proof uses uniqueness to derive them from the constructed one.

rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.FullSupportConclusion
rows.plain: Full Stieltjes support, strict increase and moment identities on [0,1)
rows.annotation: The support equality is required for every Stieltjes measure of $\gamma$, and `Set.univ` here means the relative time space $[0,1)$. Alongside strict increase of $\gamma$, the final clause requires $\mathbb E[u(t,X_t)^2]=t$ and $\mathbb E[a(t,X_t)^2]=1$ for every diffusion and every $0\le t<1$.

rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.full_support
rows.annotation: `hmin` is an input to `full_support`. The conclusion supplies a Stieltjes measure and an associated diffusion after the caller has provided the minimiser.

rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.IsMinimizer
rows.annotation: The quantifier in `IsMinimizer` compares the supplied parameter with every `OrderParameter` on the same Brownian system. The weak inequality allows ties in the Parisi value.

rows.name: OAI.SKValue.scalar_value_target
rows.annotation: In `ScalarValueConclusion` the two value clauses equate `groundStateValue` with the terminal Brownian pairing and the time integral of expected curvature. The minimiser and diffusion come from the scalar model.

rows.name: OAI.SKValue.ScalarValueConclusion
rows.plain: The terminal spin has Brownian correlation equal to the scalar ground-state value
rows.annotation: The equalities identify `groundStateValue` with $\mathbb E|X_1|-\int_0^1t\gamma(t)\,dt$, with $\mathbb E[U B_1]$, and with $\int_0^1\mathbb E[a(t,X_t)]\,dt$. The existentially quantified $U$ extends the slope to the martingale `gradientStopped` and is its limit almost surely and in mean square as $t\uparrow1$.

rows.name: OAI.SKValue.finite_gaussian_target
rows.plain: Shifted Gaussian approximation for a minimiser and its diffusion
rows.annotation: `FiniteGaussianConclusion` first gives convergence of the shifted Gaussian coefficient sum as the mesh is refined at fixed $T<1$. The later cutoff limit of its curvature integral gives the full value. For a one-step example in which dropping the shift doubles the coefficient sum, see Section 10.4 of the long record.

rows.name: OAI.SKValue.FiniteGaussianConclusion
rows.plain: The shifted Gaussian sums converge to the mean-curvature integral at fixed cutoff
rows.annotation: The first clause makes `normalizer` positive for all active indices $j<N$ once the mesh is fine enough. The next two clauses prescribe the mesh limit of `shiftedCoefficientSum` at fixed cutoff, then the left limit of the curvature integral at one.
